sources.ref_file_title: VZ12 - Characterizing Pseudoentropy and Simplifying Pseudorandom Generator Constructions
sources.note: Verified via ACM DL; STOC 2012, pp. 817-836.

pages.class_justification: The HILL construction invokes the one-way function only as an oracle (evaluating it on many independent inputs, hashing, and extracting Goldreich–Levin bits), and the security proof is a hybrid argument whose reduction runs any PRG distinguisher as an oracle to invert $f$. This is the canonical fully-black-box shape in the RTV04 taxonomy.
pages.statement: For every [[hash-function|one-way function]] $f$ there is a [[pseudorandom-generator|pseudorandom generator]] $G$: the construction uses $f$ only as a black box, and any efficient distinguisher of $G$'s output from uniform yields an efficient inverter for $f$ — [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]].
pages.sketch: HILL extract bits via universal hashing and the Goldreich–Levin predicate [[GL89 - A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions|GL89]] from many independent evaluations of $f$: the pair of $f(x)$ and hash values has pseudoentropy exceeding its real entropy, and hashing across many copies converts that gap into pseudorandom output. A hybrid argument turns any distinguisher into an inverter for $f$.
pages.improvements_text:
- Seed length reduced to $\tilde{O}(n^4)$ (from HILL's large polynomial), with nonadaptive, parallelizable calls to $f$, via next-block pseudoentropy — [[HRV13 - Efficiency Improvements in Constructing Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions|HRV13]]
- Simpler construction with seed length $\tilde{O}(n^3)$, via a KL-hardness characterization of pseudoentropy — [[VZ12 - Characterizing Pseudoentropy and Simplifying Pseudorandom Generator Constructions|VZ12]]
notes_to_keep: The hypothesis slug hash-function is the merged OWF/CRHF page, so the OWF node also owns collision resistance site-wide.
flags: GL89 is a component (hard-core predicate), not a co-original of OWF ⇒ PRG; kept in sources with role 'improvement' for lack of a 'component' role — the editor should cite it from the sketch, not as a second original.
The page's Notes contain the literal string 'Citations disagree across pages: [object Object]' — a migration artifact to delete.

Suspected-errors entry on impagliazzos-five-worlds line 63 lists this edge (as red-hf-to-pg-hill99) but the error concerns the 'TDPs (equivalently, PKE or OT)' clause of that paragraph, not OWF ⇒ PRG; the claim here is unaffected.
Exact improved seed lengths ($\tilde{O}(n^4)$ HRV13, $\tilde{O}(n^3)$ VZ12) are from my knowledge of the abstracts; verifier should confirm when creating the reference stubs.

sources.ref_file_title: BM26 - Secret-Key PIR from One-Way Functions
sources.note: Existing wiki reference page carries the abstract; eprint.iacr.org is egress-blocked from this environment, so bibliographic data is taken from the wiki page.

pages.class_justification: BM26 build SK-PIR from garbled circuits satisfying an uncorrelated-input-encoding property; the paper states no RTV class and I could not inspect the construction's black-box shape (eprint unreachable from this environment). Recording a class would add a claim.
pages.statement: [[hash-function|One-way functions]] imply [[single-server-private-information-retrieval#secret-key-pir-sk-pir|secret-key PIR]]: after an offline phase in which the client processes the $N$-bit database under a short secret key, each online query uses $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N} \cdot \secpar)$ communication and $O(N \cdot \poly(\secpar))$ server time; more generally, for any $N_c \cdot N_s = N$ the scheme achieves client-to-server communication $\tilde{O}(N_c)$ and server-to-client communication $N_s$ — [[BM26 - Secret-Key PIR from One-Way Functions|BM26]].
notes_to_keep: 'secret-key-pir' is an in-page section of single-server-private-information-retrieval, not its own slug.
flags: The source bullet's 'matching the minimal known lower bound' is a second, uncited claim and is not carried into the statement.

BM26 is a 2026 preprint (not yet a venue publication); the construction uses garbled circuits with an 'uncorrelated input encoding' property (point-and-permute garbling suffices) per the wiki's abstract — a sketch was omitted because the mechanism could not be verified beyond the abstract.

sources.ref_file_title: GGM86 - How to construct random functions
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
sources.note: Second link of the chain: PRG ⇒ PRF. The final link PRF ⇒ CPA-secure SKE is folklore.

sources.ref_file_title: BN00 - Authenticated Encryption Relations among Notions and Analysis of the Generic Composition Paradigm
sources.note: Canonical citation for encrypt-then-MAC, upgrading the CPA-secure scheme to CCA security; verified via Springer (DOI 10.1007/3-540-44448-3_41) and ePrint 2000/025 listings.

pages.class_justification: Every link of the chain is fully black-box: HILL's PRG uses the OWF only as an oracle, GGM's PRF uses the PRG only as an oracle, and $\Enc(k, m) = (r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ uses the PRF only as an oracle; each security reduction runs its adversary as a black box, and fully-black-box reductions compose (RTV04).
pages.statement: One-way functions suffice for CPA-secure symmetric-key encryption: any [[hash-function|OWF]] gives a PRG — [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]] — the PRG gives a PRF — [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]] — and encrypting $m$ as $(r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ for fresh random $r$ gives CPA-secure [[symmetric-key-encryption|SKE]] — folklore. CCA-secure SKE follows by combining the CPA-secure scheme with a [[message-authentication-code|MAC]] (also from the PRF) via encrypt-then-MAC — [[BN00 - Authenticated Encryption Relations among Notions and Analysis of the Generic Composition Paradigm|BN00]].
notes_to_keep: The hypothesis slug hash-function is the merged OWF/CRHF page, so the OWF node also owns collision resistance site-wide.
flags: COMPOSITE: this edge compresses a chain whose links already have their own pages (hash-function-to-prg-hill99, prg-to-prf-ggm86, prf-to-ske, mac-and-ske-to-cca-security); the repo's split rule suggests deciding whether this compressed edge should remain alongside them.

Suspected-errors entry on impagliazzos-five-worlds line 63 lists this edge (as red-hf-to-ske) but the flagged error is the 'TDPs (equivalently, PKE or OT)' clause, not OWF ⇒ SKE; the claim here is unaffected.
Encrypt-then-MAC requires a strongly unforgeable MAC for generic IND-CCA (BN00); the PRF-based fixed-length MAC satisfies this.

sources.ref_file_title: BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity
sources.authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh, Michael Riabzev
Eli Ben-Sasson, Alessandro Chiesa, Nicholas Spooner
sources.note: Component, not chronological improvement: the ROM compiler from IOPs to succinct non-interactive arguments that BBHR18 use to remove interaction. Verified via ACM DL / IACR archive (TCC 2016-B Part II, pp. 31-60).

pages.class_justification: BBHR18 state no reduction class. The non-interactive argument's knowledge soundness is proved in the random-oracle model, where soundness is unconditional relative to the oracle, so the RTV black-box axes do not apply cleanly; the standard-model interactive variant's CRHF-based reduction is not classified by the source either.
pages.model_justification: The non-interactive STARK is obtained by compiling a FRI-based IOP with the BCS transform, whose knowledge soundness is proved in the random-oracle model ([[BCS16 - Interactive Oracle Proofs|BCS16]]); instantiating the oracle with a concrete hash is heuristic. The interactive variant uses a collision-resistant hash for Merkle commitments in the standard model, so the frontmatter's `model: rom` is correct for the non-interactive (SNARK) conclusion.
pages.statement: From a [[hash-function|collision-resistant hash function]] — used for Merkle commitments, and modeled as a random oracle for non-interactivity — BBHR18 construct STARKs: transparent (no trusted setup) [[succinct-argument|succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge]] with prover time $O(T \log T)$ and proof size $O(\log^2 T)$ for a computation of size $T$ — [[BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity|BBHR18]].
pages.sketch: The computation trace is arithmetized into Reed–Solomon codewords, Merkle-committed with the hash function, and proximity-tested with the FRI protocol; compiling the resulting IOP with the BCS transform in the random-oracle model removes interaction while preserving knowledge soundness.
pages.improvements_text: - The ROM compiler from IOPs to succinct non-interactive arguments, used to remove interaction, is due to [[BCS16 - Interactive Oracle Proofs|BCS16]]
notes_to_keep: 'Security relies only on collision-resistant hash functions' in the source pages over-claims: non-interactive soundness needs the ROM, and the post-quantum claim additionally needs a QROM analysis.
The conclusion is the STARK variant, an alias/section of succinct-argument rather than its own slug.
flags: Duplicate BBHR18-sourced edges exist with different hypothesis sets (arithmetization-and-fri-fast-reed-solomon-iop-of-proximity-to-snark-bbhr18, arithmetization-to-snark-bbhr18, fri-fast-reed-solomon-iop-of-proximity-to-snark); this page substitutes CRHF for AIR+FRI as the hypothesis — the family should be reconciled.
BBHR18's venue: the wiki reference page should be checked — the paper is ePrint 2018/046 (a version appeared as 'Scalable Zero Knowledge with No Trusted Setup', CRYPTO 2019).

sources.ref_file_title: LS26 - Symmetric Attribute-Based Encryption from Minimal Hardness Assumptions
sources.note: Existence, authors, and abstract verified via web search (eprint listing + IACR news item 28546); eprint.iacr.org is egress-blocked from this environment.

pages.statement: Symmetric CP-ABE — ciphertext-policy [[attribute-based-encryption#symmetric-cp-abe|ABE]] in which the encryptor, too, must hold attributes satisfying the ciphertext policy — admits an IND-CCA2-secure open-universe construction from a [[hash-function|collision-resistant hash function]] and a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]], via linear secret sharing and polynomial interpolation, with no bilinear-map or lattice hardness assumption — [[LS26 - Symmetric Attribute-Based Encryption from Minimal Hardness Assumptions|LS26]].

Conclusion 'symmetric-cp-abe' has no slug; it is defined only in the Variations section of attribute-based-encryption.

sources.ref_file_title: BDH11 - XMSS A Practical Forward Secure Signature Scheme Based on Minimal Security Assumptions
sources.authors: Johannes Buchmann, Erik Dahmen, Andreas Hülsing
sources.note: Verified via Springer (DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-25405-5_8, pp. 117-129) and ePrint 2011/484 listings. Proves EU-CMA + forward security from a second-preimage-resistant hash function family and a PRF.

sources.authors: Daniel J. Bernstein, Andreas Hülsing, Stefan Kölbl, Ruben Niederhagen, Joost Rijneveld, Peter Schwabe
sources.note: Verified via ACM DL. Stateless variant (hypertree + FORS), standardized as SLH-DSA in FIPS 205.

pages.class_justification: XMSS calls the second-preimage-resistant hash family and the PRF only as oracles (Winternitz chains, L-trees, a Merkle tree), and the security reduction embeds a second-preimage or PRF challenge and runs any EU-CMA forger as a black box — the standard hash-based-signature proof shape.
pages.model_justification: BDH11's proof is in the standard model — the paper's stated selling point is provable security from minimal assumptions without random oracles. Parts of SPHINCS+'s concrete security analysis use the (Q)ROM.
pages.statement: Hash-based signatures need only symmetric primitives: XMSS is a practical, provably forward-secure many-time [[digital-signature#hash-based-signatures|signature scheme]] whose EU-CMA security reduces to a second-preimage-resistant [[hash-function|hash function]] family and a PRF — [[BDH11 - XMSS A Practical Forward Secure Signature Scheme Based on Minimal Security Assumptions|BDH11]]. SPHINCS+ removes the state via a hypertree of XMSS-style subtrees with the few-time signature FORS at the leaves, standardized as SLH-DSA in FIPS 205 — [[BHK+19 - The SPHINCS+ Signature Framework|BHK+19]].
pages.sketch: A Winternitz one-time key signs each message; a Merkle tree over the one-time verification keys authenticates them under a single root public key, and tweaked hash constructions let second-preimage resistance replace collision resistance.
notes_to_keep: The frontmatter conclusion slug 'xmss' names a concrete scheme with no wiki page; the edge relates named artifacts, not model objects.
flags: Conclusion object mismatch: frontmatter says 'xmss' while the H1 and body link digital-signature#hash-based-signatures; consider a hash-based-signatures variant node or renaming the edge.
The generic OWF ⇒ signatures result (Lamport/Merkle, NY89/Rom90) is a different edge and is not what this page records; this page is the concrete hash-based-signature family.
The migrated SPHINCS+ size claim (~8-50 KB) is an uncited concrete claim and was left out of the statement.

sources.ref_file_title: GMW91 - Proofs that yield nothing but their validity or all languages in NP have zero-knowledge proof systems
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Silvio Micali, Avi Wigderson

sources.note: Component: the statistically binding commitment from a PRG that instantiates GMW's commitment from any OWF.

sources.ref_file_title: HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function
sources.authors: Johan Håstad, Russell Impagliazzo, Leonid A. Levin, Michael Luby
sources.note: Component: PRG from any OWF, completing the OWF-only hypothesis.

pages.class_justification: The protocol uses a statistically binding commitment only as an oracle, and the commitment is built from any OWF via Naor's PRG-based scheme (Naor91 + HILL99), both fully black-box. Soundness is statistical, and the zero-knowledge reduction converts any distinguisher of the simulation into a commitment-hiding distinguisher, hence an OWF inverter, running it as a black box.
pages.statement: If [[hash-function|one-way functions]] exist, every language in $\classNP$ has a computational [[zero-knowledge-proof|zero-knowledge proof]] — [[GMW91 - Proofs that yield nothing but their validity or all languages in NP have zero-knowledge proof systems|GMW91]]. The protocol proves 3-colorability using a statistically binding commitment scheme, which any OWF provides — [[Naor91 - Bit commitment using pseudorandomness|Naor91]], [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]].
pages.sketch: The prover commits to a uniformly permuted 3-coloring of the graph; the verifier picks a random edge and the prover opens its two endpoints, which must be distinctly colored. Sequential repetition drives the soundness error $1 - 1/|E|$ down; a simulator that guesses the challenged edge and rewinds gives computational zero knowledge.
notes_to_keep: The conclusion is 'ZK proofs for all of NP', a language-class-qualified object the flat slug zero-knowledge-proof cannot express.
flags: GMW91's own theorem assumes a secure commitment/encryption; the OWF-only hypothesis follows by instantiating the commitment via Naor91 + HILL99, which postdate the conference version — this is standard citation practice and the statement is written accordingly.
The frontmatter class fully-black-box is retained and justified from the construction shape; RTV04 does not formally treat ZK-for-NP as a primitive, so the classification is informal.

sources.ref_file_title: DPSZ12 - Multiparty Computation from Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption
sources.authors: Ivan Damgård, Valerio Pastro, Nigel P. Smart, Sarah Zakarias
sources.note: SPDZ. Verified via Springer (DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-32009-5_38, pp. 643-662) and ePrint 2011/535 listings.

sources.ref_file_title: BDOZ11 - Semi-homomorphic Encryption and Multiparty Computation
sources.authors: Rikke Bendlin, Ivan Damgård, Claudio Orlandi, Sarah Zakarias
sources.note: Earlier: preprocessing from semi-homomorphic (additively homomorphic) encryption, UC-secure against a dishonest majority. Verified via IACR archive / ACM DL (EUROCRYPT 2011, pp. 169-188).

pages.class_justification: SPDZ uses a concrete SHE scheme with distributed decryption and zero-knowledge proofs of plaintext knowledge — not an arbitrary HE scheme as an oracle — and neither source states an RTV class.
pages.statement: The offline phase of preprocessing-model [[secure-multi-party-computation|MPC]] can be instantiated from somewhat [[homomorphic-encryption|homomorphic encryption]]: SPDZ generates authenticated Beaver multiplication triples by depth-1 homomorphic evaluation under a shared SHE key with distributed decryption, giving an actively secure dishonest-majority protocol (up to $n-1$ of $n$ corruptions) whose online phase is unconditionally secure — [[DPSZ12 - Multiparty Computation from Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption|DPSZ12]]. An earlier protocol obtains the preprocessing from semi-homomorphic (additively homomorphic) encryption — [[BDOZ11 - Semi-homomorphic Encryption and Multiparty Computation|BDOZ11]].
pages.sketch: Parties encrypt random shares under a joint SHE public key, multiply ciphertexts homomorphically, and jointly decrypt to obtain additively shared, MAC-authenticated triples; the online phase consumes the triples to evaluate the arithmetic circuit information-theoretically.
flags: Hypothesis 'he' is coarser than the theorem: DPSZ12 needs an SHE scheme supporting one multiplication plus distributed decryption and ZK proofs of plaintext knowledge; the wiki's HE node conflates PHE/SWHE/FHE, so the edge overstates generality.
Conclusion 'mpc-with-preprocessing' is a section anchor of secure-multi-party-computation, not its own slug.
The disjunctive sibling ot-extension-to-mpc-with-preprocessing-spdz-etc covers the other branch of the same migrated sentence — correctly split as separate pages.

sources.ref_file_title: BL13 - Limits of Provable Security for Homomorphic Encryption
sources.note: The rerandomization result verified via web search of the ECCC TR12-156 / CRYPTO 2013 abstract: a STRONG (distribution-preserving) homomorphic evaluator for essentially any boolean function (excluding trivial ones, NOT, AND, OR) converts into a rerandomization algorithm.

pages.class_justification: BL13 state no reduction class; the rerandomizer runs the scheme's homomorphic evaluator, but the paper does not classify the transformation.
pages.statement: A public-key bit [[homomorphic-encryption|encryption scheme]] with a strong — distribution-preserving — homomorphic evaluator for essentially any boolean function (excluding constants, NOT, AND, and OR) yields rerandomizable encryption: a procedure converting any ciphertext into one statistically close to independent and identically distributed with the original — [[BL13 - Limits of Provable Security for Homomorphic Encryption|BL13]]. BL13 use rerandomization to bound the provable security of such schemes.
notes_to_keep: The migrated chain's second arrow (rerandomizable encryption → SZK ≠ BPP) is BL13's barrier content and belongs on a separate barrier page, not on this construction edge.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: the unqualified edge 'HE ⇒ RE' over-claims. BL13's rerandomization lemma requires a STRONG (distribution-preserving) homomorphic evaluator — a hypothesis that compact/noise-based HE and FHE schemes need not satisfy — and no generic transformation from arbitrary HE is known. The statement adds the load-bearing qualifier; the hypothesis node should be qualified or the edge re-scoped, else demoted to wrong_claim.

BL13 is chiefly a barrier paper (no provable security beyond AM ∩ coAM via adaptive reductions, or beyond SZK via constant-query reductions, for schemes with weak/compact homomorphic evaluation of 'sensitive' function collections); a companion barrier page would capture its main theorems.
Direct fetches of eprint/ECCC are egress-blocked from this environment; verification is via search-result snippets of the abstract.

pages.class_justification: The IBE scheme is the HIBE scheme run at depth 1 with $\Delegate$ discarded — the construction uses the HIBE only as an oracle — and the security reduction forwards any IBE adversary verbatim as a depth-1 HIBE adversary with identical advantage.
pages.statement: Every [[hierarchical-identity-based-encryption|HIBE]] scheme yields an [[identity-based-encryption|IBE]] scheme: restrict identities to depth-1 vectors and discard $\Delegate$; the syntax and the IND-ID-CPA/IND-ID-CCA games then coincide, so any IBE adversary is a depth-1 HIBE adversary with the same advantage — folklore.
notes_to_keep: 'strictly generalizes' on the HIBE page additionally asserts a separation (IBE does not imply HIBE), which is neither cited nor recorded as a barrier — out of scope for this edge.
